title: Cartesian base changes of a fixed family
statement: Let $p:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. A base-change record for $p$ is a pair of schemes $X',S'$, morphisms $p':X'\to S'$, $g:X'\to X$ and $b:S'\to S$, and the assertion that the square with these four maps is cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Thus it retains a chosen cartesian family and its maps to the original family, rather than only an isomorphism class of fibre products. The identity record has $X'=X$, $S'=S$, $p'=p$, $g=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $b=\mathrm{id}_S$. The historical name FlatLCIBaseChange imposes no flatness, lci, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0E2Y, cartesian base-change squares; the record retains the maps of a chosen square and includes the identity square.
